This Exhibit B, Part 2 (Sponsor's Functional Requirements) defines the general and specific requirements for the Works in addition to the requirements in given in Exhibit B, Part 1, which is a strict copy of the Saudi Aramco and SEC technical specifications of the Master Offtake Agreement, of Fadhili Combined Heat and Power Plant (FCHPP). This Exhibit B, Part 2 must also be read in conjunction with the terms and conditions of the Agreement.
The intent of this specification is to define the scope of Works and activities to be undertaken under an Engineering Procurement and Construction (EPC) term sheet to procure for the Owner a modern, functional, well-designed power station meeting the performance requirements and being capable of continuous, efficient and reliable operation of the Plant with minimum maintenance.
The overall plant and individual systems and equipment supplied by the Contractor shall be of proven, robust and reliable design with appropriate levels of redundancy and factors of safety built-in and incorporate protective systems and devices.
It is not the intent of this specification to define all details of design and construction of the complete Works. However, it shall be recognised that the whole of the Works shall conform in all respects to high standards of engineering, design and workmanship, be in accordance with Good Industry Practices and shall be capable of performing in continuous commercial operation with very high availability whilst meeting the Contractor's guarantees and complying with all environmental and statutory regulations. No defect, error or omission in this document in relation to any design, specification or method set out herein shall relieve Contractor from his responsibility to provide a fully operational power generation Plant capable of delivering the defined capacities over the specified range of operating conditions.
In the event of any conflict with the requirements of Exhibit B, Part 2 SFR (Sponsor's Functional Requirements) and Exhibit B, Part 1 (Technical Specifications), Exhibit B, Part 1 will take precedence.
label: text

chunks.text:
The Contractor shall provide a Plant designed to meet all design requirements and conditions given in this Exhibit B and elsewhere in the Agreement.
The entire design and manufacture shall conform to the best current engineering practice to provide high availability and reliability of power, steam and water at minimum cost. Each of the several parts of the Plant shall be of the manufacturer's standard design, provided that this design is in general accordance with this Exhibit B and the Agreement and shall use components proven to be satisfactory by previous experience.
The design dimensions and materials of all parts shall be such that they will not suffer damage as a result of stresses under the most severe service conditions. The materials used in the construction of the Plants shall be of the highest quality and selected particularly to meet the duties required of them. The plants shall be designed and constructed to minimise corrosion. Workmanship and general finish shall be of the highest class throughout.
All equipment shall be designed to minimize the risk of fire and damage that may be caused in the event of fire.
The equipment shall also be designed to prevent ingress of all vermin, accidental contact with electrical live parts and minimize the ingress of dust and dirt.

The Contractor shall demonstrate during the design with necessary details and references of the recorded operational reliability of the key equipment and systems to be provided.
Throughout the design phase the Contractor shall take into account in his design the independency of each Group (if applicable) from the other groups and avoid any design leading to 'single point' failure causing the shutdown of the whole Plant or loss of total power, steam and water generation.
The Plant shall be designed to achieve a high degree of reliability and availability and such that the impact of a failure of any single piece of auxiliary equipment on the output of the Plant will be minimal.

The Plant shall endure throughout its service life the load changes defined in such a manner that no stresses exceeding the permissible limits will be caused in the components. The Plant shall be matched to the application so that with operation and maintenance in accordance with Good Industry Practice, an operational life of 25 years can be achieved from COD. A minimum Design life criteria of at least 25 years (from COD) shall be applied to materials operating in the creep region (pressure parts, steam turbine, gas turbine, HRSG, Reserve boiler, main steam piping etc.,…)
The Contractor shall state and specify the calculated number of Warm/Hot/Cold starts throughout the plant life incorporated in his design reflecting the assumed operation regime of the Plant.
Number of Plant starts in combined cycle mode per year for the Plant design shall be, as a minimum, as follows:
- maximum 60 starts per year for the water-steam cycle equipment (incl. HRSGs, steam turbine, and condenser) out of which, on average per Gas Turbine:
- -10 cold starts per year
- -18 warm starts per year
- -28 hot starts per year
- number of starts per year for the GTs: according to the Long Term Services Agreement (LTSA)
The Contractor shall use such design criteria as to enable a Plant operation of 25 years (from COD), assuming an operation and maintenance plan in accordance with the operating regime as proposed by the Contractor in this Agreement, the O&M Manuals and/or Good Industry Practice where this Agreement and/or the relevant O&M Manuals are silent. Without prejudice to main body of this Agreement, it is understood that certain components or parts thereof (including but not limited to parts of the turbines) are subject to wear and tear and/or usually have a shorter life span, thereby requiring servicing and/or replacement on a more frequent basis.

Contractor shall use KKS in order to make the identification compatible with the MMS. No alternate identification system is permitted.
All major equipment shall also be identified by name plates indicating manufacturer's name, type of equipment, serial number, construction year and main design data.
A consistent system of labelling shall be proposed by the Contractor for the approval of the Owner's Representative. The proposed material, size and exact inscription as well as proposals for the arrangement shall be submitted to the Owner's Representative for approval.
The labels shall be written in English. Warning and safety notices shall be in Arabic and English.
Safe Working Load indications on lifting equipment shall be in Arabic and English and in S.I. units.
A piping identification system subject to Owner's Representative's approval shall be applied for the Plant piping using colour strips around the pipes, as well as arrows showing flow direction.
A labelling system for the cables, control panels and instrumentation, shall be provided and shall be submitted to the Owner's Representative's for its approval .

The gas turbine shall be capable of being automatically unloaded from the full load, disconnected from the grid and shut down safely with an automatic sequence.
The GT shall be newly manufactured and shall be complete with ancillary plant, and shall comply with the following requirements:
The GT shall be located outdoors in weatherproof acoustic enclosures and shall be of the Gas fired, heavy duty, industrial, single shaft type directly coupled to a 60Hz generator.
The GT shall be capable of start-up, shutdown and continuous operation on both Sales Gas and Low BTU Gas throughout their complete range. Refer to Exhibit B, Part 1 for the fuel specifications.
The GT shall be provided with ultra-dry low NOx combustion systems for burning Sales Gas and Low BTU Gas. The GT shall comply with the emissions requirements specified elsewhere in Exhibit B, Part 1.
The GT control system shall incorporate an interface with the DCMS to facilitate integrated control of HRSGs throughout all operational manoeuvres.
GT shall also be capable of coming to rest without bearing or other damage on loss of cooling water or main AC power to its oil systems.
Permanent equipment for both on-load and off-load compressor cleaning shall be provided for gas turbine, allowing for the connection of common mobile washing equipment. One set of mobile washing equipment shall be supplied at each site. The Contractor shall detail on-load and offload procedures for wet cleaning of compressor.
The GT shall be equipped with either Start up motor or Static Start system. The gas turbine shall be provided with a full set of automatic control and protection equipment incorporating governor, temperature control and supervisory functions. Vibration levels shall conform with the ISO standard 10816, Zone B. ISO 7919 zone A/B can be used as a guideline. GT OEM package will meet A/B boundary +25% as stated in DIN ISO 7919-4 Acceptance criteria (Section 4).
The GT shall be equipped with turbine inlet air cooling by means of an evaporative cooler
Lifting gear, such as lifting beams, slings, jacks etc. required for removing complete compressor-turbine rotor, generator rotor, combustion and not gas parts, the upper portion of casings and other heavy equipment shall be provided. Turning gear system shall also be capable of manual turning.
Means shall be provided for powered turning of the rotors for a sufficient period following normal or emergency shutdown to ensure satisfactory cooling of components. The turning gear shall be interlocked such that loss of lubricating oil shall immediately stop the gear. It shall not be possible to start the turning gear without adequate lubrication oil supplies.
Jacking facilities shall be provided for all turbine and generator bearings if necessary.

The gas turbine intake air filtration system shall consist of minimum two stage filters and of the pulse-clean type. The type of filter element selected shall be capable of operating without maintenance for a minimum two-year period before a media change is required as per manufacturer's standards under normal ambient and operating conditions and under all conditions as specified in Exhibit B, Part 1. It shall be possible to operate the pulse-clean system without shutting down or reducing power output on the associated unit. In case of GT shutdown, the pulse cleaning shall be from the Plant compressed air system. Necessary design and interconnection shall be made by the Contractor.
The selection and design of the air filtration system shall be such as to ensure that sand, water droplets, dust and other harmful contaminants in the ambient air be filtered to a level which will not be detrimental to the life of the gas turbine unit under the most adverse ambient conditions at the plant site when the plant is operating continuously at maximum output with the necessity for blade cleaning reduced to a minimum.
The number of access points and penetrations into the air inlet system for maintenance and inspection shall be minimised. Any door or hatch shall be capable of being securely air-tight locked, and interlocks shall be provided to prevent any attempted start with any door or hatch not properly closed.

Heat recovery steam generator (HRSG) shall be complete with ducting, chimneys, mountings, integral valves and pipes and all other items associated with the unit to allow reliable operation.
The HRSGs shall be of proven design and in accordance with the requirements of relevant ASME standards where applicable or equivalent international standard. The HRSG shall be ASME stamped. The HRSGs shall incorporate supplementary firing for meeting the steam requirements as set forth in Exhibit B, Part 1. HRSG shall be entirely suitable for the exhaust gas temperatures and mass flow rates of the gas turbine resulting after supplementary firing (at full load and all required loads and ambient conditions).
The HRSGs and all associated facilities (e.g. Gas supply system, steam supply system etc.) shall therefore be capable of accommodating the following operating cases:
- continuous operation of HRSG without supplementary firing
- continuous operation of HRSG with minimum supplementary firing enabling fast increase of steam generation
- within design limits operation of supplementary firing according to steam demand by steam generation control or by steam pressure control; continuous operation of HRSG with maximum supplementary firing
The HRSG shall be designed for cold end corrosion issues and so that exhaust gas temperature is above the acid dew point when the gas turbine is fired on Gas.
Inspection doors and platforms shall be provided to allow ready access to the HRSG gas path, tubing and other pressure parts.
Gas duct linings and insulation shall use materials with proven capability at the maximum gas temperatures anticipated, together with design margin to allow for uneven temperature distribution downstream of supplementary firing burners. The duct geometry downstream of the supplementary firing burners shall be designed so as to ensure that no direct flame impingement on heat exchange surfaces or other metallic surfaces can occur.
The pinch point for the HRSGs shall be optimised at the design point and shall be less than 36 0 F (20 0 C).
The HRSGs shall be designed for outdoor installation and all equipment and mountings shall be entirely weather-proof and suitable for the aggressive environment. The main pressure parts shall be arranged in the form of a self-contained construction and shall be of the self-draining, horizontal gas pass type.
The water side of the HRSG shall be chemical/acid cleaned after completion of erection in accordance with accepted chemical cleaning procedures.
Regarding HRSG pressure retaining parts material selection shall be in line with requirements and stipulations of ASME I (pressure vessels) and ASME B31.1 (power piping).
All fleet wide modifications in design and construction recommended by the HRSG manufacturer after award of the Contract up to Plant final takeover shall be immediately informed to the Owner and the Contractor shall implement the same free of cost and without any time impact to the Owner. Boiler and superheater safety valves for all steam circuits shall be provided and shall be specified in accordance with design code recommendations. Each safety valve shall be fitted with its own vent-pipe, silencer and suitable drain and shall be designed and constructed to prevent back-pressure from interfering with the proper operation of the valve. The safety valves shall be designed and installed according to ASME Section I
An electrically operated relief valve shall be provided on the HP steam main before boiler stop valve for the purpose of venting steam during start-up and pressure excursions. This valve may discharge into the silencer of one of the safety relief valves as long as this does not impair the operation of the safety relief valve. The electrically operated safety relief valve is in addition to spring operated safety relief valve before boiler stop valve.
One electric motor or hydraulically operated stop valve and one non-return valve, together with one motor operated drain valve shall be installed in all main steam lines. Main steam stop valve shall be provided with a smaller electric motor operated by-pass valve or other integral means to enable downstream warming and pressure equalisation. High pressure steam from the boilers shall be routed to steam headers to the FGP interface point.
Double isolation valves operating as master/martyr shall be provided on all boiler emptying, venting and drain lines. Main vent and drain valves shall be motorised for remote operation. In the case where motor operated drain/vent valves are provided, there will be one motorised valve and one manual valve in series.
All pressurised main drains in the boiler area shall be connected to the HRSG blowdown vessel/tank.
Adequate access doors and access platforms shall be provided in the upper and lower sections of the HRSG for internal inspection.

The system provided shall be complete with provision of hard-wired level indication in the central control room.
Dedicated drum level measurements shall be provided for drum level control which will also use steam flow and feed flow meters and temperature and pressure compensation appropriate to maintaining control of level within the defined range under all operating conditions and transients in normal operation.

Each HRSG shall have a single flue stack of > 60m height, subject to confirmation by Saudi Aramco/Owner based on the air emissions assessment. The diameter shall be such that it is self-sustaining, i.e. its lift due to temperature differential shall be equal to or greater than the sum of all losses.
The stacks shall be designed and constructed in accordance with DIN, EN, BS or ASME STS-1 or an equivalent approved standard if acceptable as per Exhibit B, Part 1. The stacks shall be provided with suitable earthling bosses and earthed.
The stacks shall be clad and insulated where required for personnel protection. Optionally expanded metal instead of insulation can also be provided where required for personnel protection in the Stacks. The style and finish shall be as approved by the Owner. Alternatively; the main stack can be insulated up to the stack damper if similar references in Saudi Arabia are provided by the Contractor and is as per the relevant standards.
The efflux velocity shall not be less than 15m/sec at normal operating loads (60-100% GT load with or without supplementary firing) and shall be designed throughout the life of the Plant.
Aircraft warning lights as required shall be provided on the Stacks to meet local regulations.
Provision shall be made for the permanent monitoring of stack outlet gas emissions in accordance with environmental requirements specified in Exhibit B, Part 1. In addition, the stack shall be provided with test points at positions such that the distribution and temperature of the exhaust gas can be determined in accordance with the agreed test code.

The duct and casing part of the HRSG shall be insulated internally. It shall also make possible the bypass operation of each steam turbine feeding directly the FGP. It shall also ensure the HRSGs stability during start and stop and when a turbine trip or the load rejection occurs or when the Plant is running on ST bypass mode.
With the common header configuration feeding both steam turbines, the proper heating measures for cold start of one ST rest of the plant being in full operation shall be provided.
Each GT shall be capable of continuous operation in combined cycle mode also in case of a part of the other GTs are not in operation. The stopping and start-up of one GT/HRSG unit while any of the other GT/HRSG unit(s) remain(s) in combined cycle mode shall be possible and is a normal operation mode. Specific steam by-pass station is to be provided to enable smooth start-up/stop of a GT/HRSG unit when the other unit(s) is (are) already in operation.

The capacity and design of the ST bypass system shall enable continuous GT operation at base load also in the event ST has been tripped and/or when the ST is not in operation. The design of the bypass system, bypass valves and their control capability shall control a smooth LP steam pressure transient in the event of ST trips (and all scenarios 1-11 as mentioned in Exhibit B, Part 1) in order to continue to feed the FGP.
The bypass system shall include fast action isolating valves, pressure reducing valves with de-superheating sections and modulating valves with atomizers for injection of spray water.
The by-pass system shall be operated automatically during startup/shutdown, in the event of a trip or sudden ST load reduction or in case of lower electrical demand. They shall be dedicated special bypass valves specifically designed for steam bypass applications with hydraulic or pneumatic actuation. The steam turbine bypass controls shall be integrated with the overall Plant DCMS.
The Contractor shall indicate in his proposal his successful experience in using bypass systems of similar design and shall indicate the design aspects that prevent damage from vibration, thermal shock, and pressure waves resulting from shock waves at the different pressure reduction stages and pressure reducing valve instabilities. Special attention shall be given to effective vibration damping design measures.

The Reserve Boiler shall be of proven design and in accordance with the requirements of relevant ASME standards where applicable such as ASME I (pressure vessels) and ASME B31.1 (power piping) and shall be ASME certified. The Reserve Boiler(s) shall provide reliable and consistent performance to the operating parameters as defined in Exhibit B, Part 1.
The reserve boiler shall have dual fuel capability to fire both Low BTU and Sales gas, all inherit safety devices, an individual CEMS and meet the emission and stack limits as per Exhibit B, Part 1. Forced draft fans shall provide necessary combustion air. Feedwater shall be supplied from the deaerator via a dedicated feedwater pump. The reserve boiler shall be kept in warm standby as per Exhibit B, Part 1 when in stand-by with a steam bleed from the main steam system.
Inspection doors and platforms shall be provided to allow ready access to the Reserve Boiler's gas path, tubing and other pressure parts.
Gas duct linings and insulation shall use materials with proven capability at the maximum gas temperatures anticipated.
The Reserve Boiler(s) shall be designed for outdoor installation and all equipment and mountings shall be entirely weather-proof and suitable for the aggressive environment.
The water side of the Reserve Boiler(s) shall be chemical/acid cleaned after completion of erection in accordance with accepted chemical cleaning procedures.
Materials operating in the creep region shall have a minimum design life criteria of at least 25 years (from COD).
All modifications in design and construction recommended by the Reserve Boiler(s)' manufacturer after award of the Contract up to Plant final takeover shall be immediately informed to Saudi Aramco and the Contractor shall implement the same free of cost and without any time impact to the Owner. Contractor shall provide correction curves for gross power output of the Steam turbine versus ambient conditions of dry bulb temperature and relative humidity. In addition, the ACC shall be capable of handling steam turbine bypass operation during start-up, shut-down and/or emergencies (shall include a reserve of at least 10% to cover possible steam turbine overloads). The orientation and layout of the ACC shall be such that the adequate air circulation is possible around the ACC.
Each ACC fan shall be individually isolatable. Access ways, galleries, platforms and ladders shall be provided for safe and efficient operation and maintenance including maintenance of fans, gearboxes, bearings etc. The ACC shall comprise a number of cells mounted on a hot dip galvanised steel support structure. Internal partition walls shall be located between each fan section to reduce mal-distribution of air flow. Lockable access doors shall be provided in the partition walls (normally kept closed and locked).
The ACC shall be of proven design with supplier references demonstrating the same. The ACC shall be designed for full vacuum to an approved heat exchanger design code as applicable such as Heat Exchanger Institute (HEI) Standards for Steam Surface Condensers, ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code etc.
The ACC shall be of the forced draught type, located on a steel structure at ground level. It shall be capable of condensing steam from the steam turbine and turbine drain flash vessel (if provided) at all ambient conditions and at all loads.
The ACC shall be arranged to minimise the recirculation of cooling air.
During steam turbine trip transient/start-up phase, the whole steam flow from the by-pass system will be discharged to the ACC.
During the by-pass conditions, the ACC shall be able to maintain the pressure such that no limitation occurs for the steam turbine capabilities.
In addition to the requirements of Exhibit B, Part 1; the ACC shall be designed to be capable of condensing the entire steam flow dumped by the by pass system following a steam turbine trip, for indefinite time.
Finned tubed bundles shall be used within the ACC. The tube fin material combination shall be of Welded carbon steel tube + carbon steel fins (both hot dipped galvanized). In case Contractor proposes Aluminium coated (Aluminized steel) tubing with Aluminium fins then the same is acceptable only for single row type condensers.
Wind walls shall be installed around the perimeter of the ACC structure, minimally extending from fan deck level to the top of the heat exchanger bundles. Each ACC shall be equipped with systems such as high pressure spray to enable cleaning of the outer surfaces of the tubes.
Fans shall be of single-speed type. The Contractor shall develop the operating concept for ACC during the detailed design phase.

The ACC shall be arranged together with condensate extraction pumps, condensate control valve including a bypass control valve with manual valve, in addition to steam (if applicable) and water side isolating valves. The ACC shall be arranged to operate automatically.
The design and workmanship shall be such that the pumps are readily assembled or dismantled and that they shall operate satisfactorily under all operating conditions without undue wear, vibration and cavitation.
The pumps and motors shall be located at ground floor level outdoors and close to the ACC condensate tank. The configuration must be based on the optimal suction requirements.
Basket strainer with fine mesh/screen shall be supplied on the pump suction to remove suspended solids in the condensate, particularly during start-up (commissioning period). After commissioning this shall be replaced by the Contractor with coarse mesh / screen.
In case load restrictions or damages to the ACC are observed before the end of the warranty period while the plant is operated within the specified design range, the Contractor shall improve the design with adequate means (e.g. wind screens, different fan design, etc) to avoid such restrictions or damages, at no cost to the Owner. The proposed corrective actions and the timing of installation shall be subject to Owner's approval.
An ACC cleaning system should be included.
The contractor should provide correction curves of ACC performance in function of wind velocity, direction and ambient temperature.

An integrated structure carrying the condenser, fans and motors, plenum chamber, access galleries, staircases, platforms and maintenance runway beams shall be supplied and secured to ground foundation concrete supports. Steelwork, platforms, ladders and stairways shall be hot dip galvanized.
The height of the structure shall take account of the air velocity when operating with all fans in service. The ACC shall be designed with a fan deck at least 16m high to minimize air recirculation.
The structural steelwork shall be capable of supporting the ACC at all operating, maintenance and testing loads and shall comply with the wind speed design loadings given for the Site. Where stress analysis calculations are performed, the location of anchors, guides or restraints shall be based on the results of the final stress analysis. Such anchors, guides and restraints shall be designed for the maximum forces and moments encountered.
The civil engineering and structural works shall be designed in accordance with accepted codes and standards of skill, care and diligence.
The seismic design, both for structural sizing and operating behavior, shall comply with the minimum seismic requirements provided in Exhibit B, Part 1.
The design, fabrication, testing, installation and fixing method of all steelwork including structural members, checker plate flooring, handrailing, ladders, open grid flooring and stair treads shall be in accordance with recognized codes and standards for steelwork.
The necessary signalizations shall be foreseen.
Stairs shall be preferred to ladders wherever possible. Where ladders are used they shall be installed only in areas where only occasional access is required or where space limitations so dictate.

Rotating parts and relevant transmission components shall be designed to limit the noise according to the environmental regulations and as specified in Exhibit B-Part 1, whichever is more stringent.
Each cell shall have a motor driven forced draught fan driven by an electric motor, connected to the reduction gear by a shaft. Fan electric motors shall have half shrouded, stay put, emergency stop buttons located within 5m of the motor location. These buttons shall require a key to reset. 3NC contacts are required (230VAC or 220VDC insulated)
The electric motors shall be totally enclosed and fan cooled, fitted with lubricated antifriction bearings and moisture resistant insulation, designed for continuous outdoor service, with mechanical protection IP55 as a minimum, insulation Class F.
The motor and the reduction gear shall be designed in order to withstand the maximum electrical power with adequate margin.
Platform and ladders must be made to allow periodical check, lubrication of motor bearings and of gearbox bearings.
The motors will be selected taking into account the driven load characteristic; the motors will have at least a 10% operating margin on power output.

chunks.text:
The feedwater pumps shall comply with the requirements of Exhibit B, Part 1.
The boiler feedwater pumps shall be capable of supplying the maximum continuous rating water flow to each drum, at a pressure 3 percent higher than the setting of HRSG drum safety valve.
Suction and discharge isolation valves and a non-return discharge valve shall be installed for each pump. Each pump shall be protected during periods of low flow with independent, minimum flow recirculation paths returning to the feedwater tank. The energy of the recirculation fluid shall be reduced through a pressure drop across the minimum flow valve and through an orifice/backpressure device located at the inlet to the feedwater tank. The minimum flow valve shall be designed for severe service, with provisions to minimize cavitation. The orifice/backpressure device shall prevent flashing in the recirculation piping downstream of the minimum flow valve.
Each pump shall be fitted with a suction strainer complete with manual blowdown. Strainers shall be equipped with commissioning and operating inserts. The strainer shall have differential pressure indication, with automatic pump changeover on high strainer differential pressure alarm.
Vibration monitoring and protection shall be provided.
A transient analysis shall be performed for the pump suction to ensure that the feedwater tank volume, elevation, suction line sizing, and layout maintain net positive suction head (NPSH) at all times and loads.
The pumps shall withstand any possible thermal shock without damage or leakage. The operating speed range of the pumps shall avoid all natural structural resonances. All parts of the pump in contact with feed water shall be corrosion resistant steel. Cooling of the feed water pumps and auxiliaries shall be provided by the closed cycle cooling water system.

chunks.text:
Refer to Exhibit B -Part 1.
The condensate system includes return from the ACCs and also from the FGP. Condensate return from the ACCs shall mix with FGP return condensate which has been treated in the CPP. The final condensate shall be directed to the deaerator/feedwater tanks (with consideration of balancing the water in each water/steam cycle if necessary).
FGP return condensate is at high temperature (<100°C) and must be cooled prior to entering the CPP. A Fin Fan Cooler shall be considered with N+2 modules where any one module can be isolated for repair without impacting the full condensate flow. The fin fan cooler shall be designed to meet CPP inlet temperature requirements of 60 °Cat design conditions.
Because the FGP condensate return temperature is <100°C, it is not possible to consider the condensate storage tank as part of the normal operating cycle as the water will flash if it goes to atmospheric pressure. Condensate storage tank should therefore be connected either before or after the CPP where the condensate temperature is low. Additionally; condensate storage should be connected away from the normal path of the condensate.
The condensate coming from the ACC and from the condensate polishing system shall be directed to the deaerator/feedwater tanks (with consideration of balancing the water in each water/steam cycle if necessary).

The Gas conditioning and filtering skid shall include carbon steel filters/separators installed downstream of Plant Gas Delivery Point. The filters/separators shall be fabricated per ASME VIII to remove solid particles of micron size 3µ with an efficiency of 100% filtrate rate and 0.5µ at 99.5% or better and liquid particles of micron size 3µ with an efficiency of 100% filtrate rate and 0.3µ at 99.5% or better, to the requirements of the gas turbine equipment supplier. Liquid drain from the filter separators shall be routed to the fuel gas condensate drain tank from where it will be truckloaded out for disposal. Level-indicating transmitters and switches shall provide level indication to the control room operator. The isolation valves for filter separators shall be double seat ball valves.
Gas pressure control stations shall be provided for each of the Plant power and steam Unit. The Gas pressure to the Plant power and steam units shall be controlled within the appropriate operating range via pneumatically operated control valves. The pressure control station shall be provided with necessary control valves. A pneumatically operated highpressure shutoff valve will also be provided to close upon high downstream Gas pressure and will minimize the amount of Gas vented to atmosphere when the safety relief valve lifts. Triple redundant pressure transmitters shall be provided downstream of the regulating station to provide a highly reliable Gas pressure control system that will minimize unnecessary turbine trips. The Gas System shall be provided with ESD valves upstream to the fuel gas system.
Extended capacity strainer shall be provided to remove impurities from the Gas. A pressure switch shall monitor the differential across the strainers will signal an alarm to the central control room via DCMS for the pressure drop across the strainer indicates cleaning is required.
If required, Gas heaters and heating water boosting pumps shall be provided in order to control Gas temperature to maintain variation of Modified Wobbe Index (MWI) within +/- 5% to enable the gas turbines to operate at full load for both the Gas qualities within the specified ranges in Exhibit B, Part 1.
Scrubbers shall be provided to remove liquid inside fuel gas. In case the gas pressure is lower than heating liquid, scrubbers will also be installed downstream to the fuel gas heaters to prevent any moisture carry over from any tube leak in fuel gas heater. Liquid drain from the scrubber shall be routed to a fuel gas scrubber condensate drain tanks from where it will be truck-loaded out for disposal.
For each gas turbine, 2 coalescent final filters (2 x 100%) shall be foreseen (if required by the gas turbine manufacturer).
Piping after last scrubber to gas turbine shall be of stainless steel, if recommended by the manufacturer.

Each chemical dosing system shall comprise all equipment for the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the dosing systems, including bunds, segregated chemical drains, appropriate ventilation and emergency eye wash and deluge shower units.
Each chemical dosing system shall consist of two (2) x 100% chemical dosing pumps and one (1) chemical dosing tank.
The chemical dosing tank shall combine solution mixing and preparation and shall be made of stainless steel or synthetic material. It shall have a working capacity of 4 days of continuous use for each additive. The tank shall be provided with electric agitator as necessary.
The dosing pumps material shall be AISI 316L (1.4404) for the casing. Two (2) pumps per chemical shall be provided.
Injection pipes and valves are made of stainless steel AISI 316L (1.4404).
Bulk storage for each chemical shall be provided with a storage capacity of at least 7 days with the Plant at full load. For chemicals in liquid or gaseous state bulk storage tanks sized to unload a full standard road tanker shall be provided Plus 4 day's storage capacity. Each control air receiver shall have sufficient capacity to enable the Plant to be shut down in a safe and controllable manner and enable standby compressor plant to come into operational service without reduction in air supply. The compressed air systems shall include (i) General Service Air and (ii) Control and Instrumentation Air, configured to ensure a sustained supply of compressed air to the plant.

- the product air shall:

The Contractor shall provide electric overhead travelling crane for the maintenance of the steam turbine generator units.
The crane shall be designed and constructed in accordance with the requirements of applicable mandatory local norms and standards or equivalent international standard and shall be complete in all respects for safe and efficient operation.
If required a traverse, to facilitate the separate lifting of generator stator and rotor assemblies and component parts, shall be supplied. The lifting beam shall be attached to the main hook of the crane.
The control of each crane motion will be arranged to incorporate a steady creep speed.
The crane shall be complete in every respect including access platforms, ladders, supports, protective covers, motors, control gear and wiring with main isolator and longitudinal isolated gantry conductors, collectors/supports, and longitudinal crane rails complete with holding down bolts and any other auxiliary apparatus incidental thereto for the safe and efficient operation of the crane.
A warning alarm shall be mounted on the electrically operated crane bridge in an easily accessible position. The alarm shall be initiated by the crane operator from the radio remote control to give warning of impending long travel motion.
The crane shall be fitted with a nameplate showing the manufacturer's name, the date of manufacture, a serial or identification number and the rated capacity of the crane.

Complete lifting equipment required for operation, maintenance, removal, and reinstallation of the equipment shall be designed, specified, procured, developed, fabricated, furnished, delivered, and installed.
Scope shall include turbine hall overhead travelling crane, and boiler feed pump overhead monorail(s) and the monorails in other areas required for the maintenance of the equipment, including but not limited to bridge, trolley, rail sweeps, motors, motor starters, gears, brakes, wheels, stops, bumpers, handrails, cables, wiring, panels, lighting, conductors, power feed connectors, pendant controls, radio controls, hoists, hooks, ropes, limit switches, etc., as needed to make a complete system.
The lifting access bay in the boiler structure servicing the boiler structure floors shall be provided with an electric operated controlled hoist with motor operated trolley for boiler top.
For indoor auxiliaries and machinery where the weight of a single part to be handled exceeds 10 tons, a minimum of a monorail with motorized trolley and motorized hoist shall be provided.
For indoor machines or indoor equipment, where the weight of a single part to be handled is 5 tons to 10 tons, a minimum of a monorail with geared trolley and manual hoist shall be provided and where the weight of a single part to be handled is less than 5 tons, only an overhead steel beam (monorail) or eye-plate shall be provided for supporting a temporary geared trolley and manual hoist or lifting equipment.
The bridge and gantry cranes and trolleys shall be sized to lift the heaviest piece in the equipment to facilitate their erection and maintenance. The turbine building crane shall have both main and auxiliary hooks.
The bridge and gantry crane wheel loads shall be as specified by the crane manufacturer. Impact loads from cranes shall be in accordance with AISC Standard.
Monorail hoist loads shall include lifted load, hoist weight, trolley weight and impact. Impact for monorail beams shall be 25% of the lifted load in the vertical direction. Transverse and longitudinal loads from trolley to the trolley beam shall be in accordance with trolley manufacturer's recommendation. The cranes and trolley shall have stops to prevent over travel.

In addition to the material used, also the location, correct dimensioning and quality of supports as well as flexibility of the pipework shall be taken into account when designing the piping and piping layout. Expansion bends or loops shall be provided where required.
The design of all pipes, bends and fittings shall comply with norms and standards as per Exhibit B -Part 1
Piping for high-pressure services shall be cylindrical and uniform in section.
All atmospheric blow-down lines, drains, vents, sampling lines etc. belonging to the water-steam cycle shall be equipped with double shutoff valves if pressure exceeds 40 bar(g).
When locating the valves and the measuring points (temperature sensors, pressure taps etc.) the movements of the pipes with respect to the steel construction shall be taken into consideration.
Generally, clean drains shall be returned back to the process but considering at all times the operational requirements for chemical purity of the water-steam cycle. Such drains include e.g. steam lines, turbine drains, by-pass lines etc. Alternatively, for steam line drainage between FCHPP and up to FGP interface point only, the use of steam traps with soakaway pits is acceptable
Flanges shall be the same materials as the joining pipe or fitting. Where unavoidable for dissimilar joining flanges within the GTG Package only (not applicable for interface between Contractor and GTG Package where flanges of similar material shall be used) dissimilar flanges may be used as per applicable codes.
All steam mains shall be erected with a continuous slope in the direction of the flow so that the condensed steam will flow towards the drainage points.
The pipes shall be equipped with necessary venting, draining and sampling points including valves. Venting valves shall be collected to one group and they shall be provided with drainage to the drainage tank. Subject to the approval of Saudi Aramco, warm up vent with silencer (if required) is acceptable only for steam headers between FCHPP and FGP interface point.
All HP steam stop valves shall be equipped with by-pass valves. In case Contractor is of the opinion that a bypass valve is not required for any particular valve then, the list of such valves along with sufficient technical details shall be provided to the Owner during detailed design stage for the Owner's approval.
All fire fighting system piping underground shall be in GRP or any other adequate material suitable for that function. Special caution shall be taken during installation and erection to avoid any internal tension and leaks.
The effect of water hammering shall be taken into account when designing the location of drain lines.

The piping support structure design shall be such that no harmful vibrations occur during operation of the Plant. The movements of the pipework during standstill (cold) and during the normal operation (hot) shall be taken into account. Supports shall not be welded to the bottom flange of beams.
Pipes and fittings shall be so supported that the pipes may expand and contact freely.

The Contractor shall match his pump characteristics to the pipe system network to achieve the high pump efficiency and reliability.
In normal operation, it shall be possible to start and stop the pumps under any operating conditions without any special precautions such as venting or warming.
The service life of the mechanical shaft seals shall be at least 20,000 operating hours and 40,000 operating hours for the bearings.
To avoid vibration problems all large pumps, including feedwater pumps, shall be located on separate foundations.
The impeller of the single stage pumps shall be readily withdrawable from the pump casing without the need to transfer the pump and with minimum dismantling and disconnection work from the pipework.
The pump design shall ensure that alignment is maintained between the various assemblies by recesses, spigots and dowels and shall be such that all components liable to wear can be replaced.
Components of the multistage pumps shall be permanently marked with the manufacturer's number and where dowels are not used, permanently marked for correct assembly. The pump casing and the impeller shall have detachable wear rings.
Where grease points are necessary they shall be fitted with removable screwed plugs which shall be accessible without removing guards.
Bearings with bearings which require a continuous supply of lubricant shall incorporate a means of monitoring such a supply, by temperature rise as appropriate for the type of bearing employed; separate monitors being fitted for each bearing feed or housing.
If sealing water is needed, flow shall be shown by sight glasses.
Special care in the selection of materials shall be taken in order to avoid binding and electrolytic action between the shaft sleeve and the mechanical seal components, particularly where long periods of idleness are inherent in the duty cycle as in the case of standby and storm pumping.
The highest point on the pump casing shall be fitted with a manual air release cock having a removable handle or an automatic air release valve with a lock-able isolation valve as specified (or according to the Manufacturer standard ).
When required, pumps shall have necessary hoisting and dismantling facilities, like hoisting beams, for maintenance purposes.
The test performed to verify the trouble free operation, of pumps shall at least include verification of pumps performances and validation of pumps curves including required NPSH curve, vibration measurements, etc). Saudi Aramco and/or their representative shall be informed reasonably in advance and allowed to witness the tests.

The design, structure and material of the valves shall be suitable for their particular operational purpose.
Valves and devices shall be located in an ergonomically correct way in respect to the maintenance platforms considering that maintenance shall be possible without removing the valves (except butterfly valve) from the pipe.
The valve and seat material shall comply with the operational and corrosion conditions for which they are intended.
The upper structure of the steam valves shall be designed in the manner that, at different operational temperatures of the spindle and cover, there is sufficient spindle force left to maintain the seat pressure required. In motor-controlled valves the seat force shall not vary according to the temperature so that the operating mechanism could not open cold valve.
The valves and the accessories shall be mounted so that pipe reactions do not hamper perfect valve operation and tightness.
The valves shall be well accessible for maintenance and operation. The larger valves (e.g.. boiler safety valves) must allow for the use of a crane or a hoist during maintenance. When necessary, the valve shall be equipped with an extended spindle. The valve hand-wheel shall not be higher than 1700mm above the operating level.
The following minimum data shall be permanently marked on the valve body:
- DN and PN
- material
- manufacturer's mark
- identification marks of the certificates
- flow direction
Generally (subject to Owner's Design Review and wherever they are required to be operated during start-up, shut-down and operation) stop valves larger than DN400 shall be equipped with actuators in order to enable operations from the main control room via DCMS.
Each valve must display with a clear text giving the identification number of the valve and markings of the "CLOSED-OPEN" positions with the direction arrows, and local position indicators.
The direction of rotation of valve hand-wheels (when looking at the face of the hand-wheel) shall be clockwise to close valves.
The position of all control valves shall be indicated on the DCS operating station.
The electrical valve-actuator combination has to be designed in such a way that the actuator does not damage the valve even if wrongly controlled with stall torque at 10 % overvoltage. There shall be one adjustable torque switch for both directions to prevent damage in the event of jamming.
Valve sizes shall be chosen according to pipe sizes, with the exception of control valves.
In the case of strong cavitation the control valves shall be of the multistage construction type.
The bonnets of the high-pressure (> 40barg) gate valves shall be of self-sealing construction type.
Stop valves, which operate at under pressure, must have either seal water supply, or some other system that minimises air leakage through the stem packing.
Intake and outlet nozzles of globe valves shall be located on the same centre line of the valve casing.

The electric actuators shall be provided with anti-condensation heaters when mounted outdoors.
The electric actuator shall be self-locking. The motor and control gear shall be placed in such a position relative to the valve that there is no possibility of leakage of steam or water from the valve joints or glands blowing on to the motor or control equipment. A hand operating facility shall be provided and be so arranged that the mechanism will disengage automatically when the motor operates.
The actuator shall have an adjustable mechanical position indicator so that it may readily be seen whether the valves are open or shut and in the case of those valves fitted with extended spindles, indicators shall be fitted both to the extended spindle and to the valve spindle.

All blow-out and safety valves shall be equipped with efficient silencers.

All lagging adjacent to hot surfaces shall be capable of withstanding the maximum surface temperature obtainable in service without deterioration or breakdown of the material
The valve boxes and the covers of manholes shall be easily dismantled and reinstalled. The same is also valid for the boiler parts, which shall be regularly checked. The demountable insulation boxes shall be strengthened. It shall be possible to change temperature thermo-elements without dismantling the insulation.
The penetrations of hot pipes (e.g. blow-out piping of safety valves) shall also be insulated. The risk of ignition of construction materials of the boiler/turbine house shall be taken into account, and the insulation material used shall be non-combustible.
All exposed portions of the Plant which are subject to a temperature exceeding 60°C and are likely to come in direct contact with personnel shall be provided with approved thermal insulation so that the temperature on the outside of the insulation does not exceed 60°C when the ambient temperature is 35°C.
The insulation of the boiler shall be made up of two layers of the insulating wool mat, when applicable, and the seams of the separate layers shall be overlapped. The cladding shall be aluminium sheeting. The insulation of the turbine shall be made up of either at least two layers insulation wool mat or spray-on insulation material, and it shall be covered so that it prevents moisture and oil penetration into the insulation material.
Lagging shall be properly secured in position and it shall not loosen or suffer damage when subjected to vibration. Turbine cylinders shall be provided with fixing points for the insulation.
The insulation works shall be designed so that insulation will not get wet during storage or installation.
Piping and vessels shall be insulated with prefabricated mineral wool elements. The insulation of all piping, vessels, valves and fittings shall be finally covered (e.g. aluminium for outdoor application or galvanised steel sheeting for indoor application) and completely weatherproofed on any outdoor installations.
In all cases, the use of Asbestos is forbidden.

Regardless of the requirements of the specific code or specifications applicable to the design and/or construction of the plant and associated pipework, it is a mandatory requirement of this Specification that all welds shall be subject to appropriate post weld treatment with the following exceptions:
- austenitic stainless steels
- plain carbon steels containing less than 0.25 per cent carbon at thicknesses up to and including 30 mm
- low alloy steels containing ½ per cent molybdenum and 1¼ per cent chromium, ½ per cent molybdenum up to and including thicknesses of 12.5 mm provided that:
- -a hardness traverse across the weld zone gives no single result greater than 240 hv10
- -no fillet weld leg is greater than 8 mm
- -a minimum preheat of 200°c is used for welding
Plain carbon steels shall contain no more than 0.25% carbon.
All post weld heat treatments of materials and components for use at temperatures in excess of 400°C shall be so designed as to guarantee maximum creep properties in the parent materials and weldments.
The soaking times at the selected heat treatment temperatures shall be:
- low alloy steels not containing vanadium, 5 minutes per mm of thickness with a minimum time of 120 minutes
- low alloy steels containing vanadium and high (11 to 15 per cent) chromium steels containing vanadium, 180 minutes regardless of thickness
In the event that any post weld heat treatment is carried out at a temperature in excess of the original tempering temperature of the parent materials, a re-assessment of the design strength limit stresses for the materials will be required. This may, in the absence of acceptable mechanical test data for the specific condition, require re-determination of the relevant mechanical properties of the materials.
The requirements for post weld heat treatment do not affect or replace in any way the requirements for maintenance of welding preheats or post welding heating for the purposes of diffusing hydrogen from the weldment.
Post weld heat treatment, where applicable, shall be conducted in accordance with applicable codes and standards. Records of post weld heat treatment shall be made available for inspection when requested.
After completion of welding, fabricated parts shall be stress relieved in accordance with the applicable codes and standards.
In the case of IPB welds, AWS or other relevant international Standards shall apply.

Steelwork in close proximity with hot air or gas or subject to radiation from any part of the Plant shall be adequately protected and insulated. On completion of the work, all necessary platforms, ladders and stairways for the Plant and ancillary equipment shall be provided to give safe access to all equipment, valves, and instrumentation.
Platforms shall be constructed using galvanised open steel flooring and shall cater for the relevant loading for maintenance. The flooring shall be bolted to the framework using approved bolted clips. The platform framework and the corresponding nuts and bolts shall be galvanised. The minimum width of the galleries for emergency exits and the minimum free height of these galleries shall be according to relevant standards. Exit routes shall be clearly marked with colours according to applicable norms and standards.
Platforms shall be provided around equipment as required for maintenance work, testing, inspection and safe operation. Platforms shall be sized to facilitate safe ergonomic operation of manual valves and equipment between waist and shoulder level of a standard man. Relief valves shall be grouped together and an access platform provided. Operating valves which cannot be serviced from a platform shall be operated by other approved means.
All platforms to be visited on a daily basis shall be provided with stairways, except where a permanent access ladder is the only feasible means of access. All interior and exterior platforms, gratings, checker plate, stairways and handrails shall be galvanised.
Platforms shall be constructed using galvanised open steel flooring or a suitable grade of GRP grating in areas of high salinity, to the relevant ISO, British Standards or ASME and shall cater for the relevant loadings for maintenance. The electrical equipment shall be designed to ensure continuity of operation of the main plant under all working conditions at the Plant Site. The plant shall also be capable of meeting all transient, abnormal and load shedding scenarios. In addition it shall be arranged to facilitate inspection, maintenance and repairs.
All electrical equipment shall be type and routine tested in factories. Type test will not be repeated if type test certificates of the same equipment type are available.
All reasonable precautions shall be taken in the design of equipment and of works to ensure the safety of personnel concerned with the operation and maintenance of works. Safety, isolation, locking and interlocking facilities shall comply with the relevant standards and requirements.
Electrical equipment located in hazardous areas shall be provided with special enclosures suitable for the hazard classification of the areas according to the guidelines provided in statutory regulations and codes.

Anti-condensation heaters shall be provided for motors above 20kW rating, motorized valve actuators, switchgear and control panels, except where located in air-conditioned rooms. Except for motors which have heaters operated by the motor controller, the other heaters shall be permanently connected without thermostats and energized via a local isolator supplied from a local distribution board.
Electric motors shall be designed for class F temperature rises, with acceptable temperature rises limited to class B over the entire range of ambient air temperatures.
Large motors of 1MW and above shall use high efficiency designs as far as possible.
Station Service and Unit Auxiliary transformers and switchgear shall be designed to allow normal operation with one transformer out of service. A change-over scheme shall allow transfer, without loss of output, between this running condition and normal system operation.
All MV and LV switchgears, DC switchgear equipment, batteries and charger, UPS inverters, distribution equipment and safe AC equipment shall be suitably housed inside fully air-conditioned containments.
Sunshades shall be provided for all cubicles, terminal boxes and enclosures mounted outdoors. OEM (Siemens) standard design only for GTG package for providing no sunshade is acceptable, if the equipment / enclosure is suitable designed for outdoor installation.
A digital fault monitoring and disturbance recording system shall also be provided, which shall cover the entire power station electrical system items, including
- incomers and couplers of all main low voltage (LV) switchgears
- all MV switchgear feeders except motor feeders (motors shall be monitored via the DCMS)
- all HV switchyard bays

chunks.text:
Generators shall be two pole, 60Hz designed, built and tested in accordance with IEC-60034. The generators shall have a high degree of reliability under steady state condition and shall be capable of confirming recovery under emergency conditions and during transient frequency fluctuations.
Generator shall have a short circuit ratio of not less than 0.5 and shall be capable of withstanding 1.3 times the rated voltage for 30 seconds during load rejection or similar events. The generator sub-transient reactance (saturated) shall be a minimum of 12% (IEC basis).
On line condition monitoring for stator winding insulation and search coil to detect shorting of rotor winding turns shall be provided.
Anti-condensation heaters shall be provided for air circuits, generator windings, excitation systems and control cubicles. Heaters shall be suitably sized to prevent condensation. Heaters shall be switched on automatically when the generators are taken out of service.
The generator neutral point shall be earthed through a distribution transformer and loading resistor to limit the earth fault current to a maximum of 10 Amps.
The following protection shall be provided and shall be duplicated to the extent so that at least two independent devices shall detect a fault.
- generator over excitation (ANSI code 24)
- phase under-voltage (ANSI code 27)
- generator over frequency (ANSI code 81O)
- generator under frequency (ANSI code 81U)
- stator differential (ANSI code 87G)
- overall differential (ANSI code 87TG), CT will be on neutral side
- neutral ground overvoltage (Stator Ground) (ANSI code 59N)
- current unbalance/Negative phase sequence (ANSI code 46)
- loss of excitation (ANSI code 40)
- reverse power/anti-motoring (ANSI code 32)
- monitoring and alarm of generator stator
- voltage transformer supervision (miniature circuit breakers will be used instead of fuses)
- rotor earth fault (ANSI code 64G)
- out of step (ANSI code 78)
- phase time overcurrent (ANSI code 51)
- phase overvoltage (ANSI code 59)
- stator ground protection (3 rd Harmonic) (ANSI code 27TN)
- phase distance (ANSI code 21)
- voltage restrained time overcurrent (ANSI code 51V)
- inadvertent energisation (ANSI code 50/27)
- stator earth fault stage 1 and 2 (ANSI 64-1 and 64-2)
- breaker failure protection (ANSI 50BF)
The Contractor shall include additional protection if considered necessary.
The protective relays shall be electronic digital type with selfmonitoring functions for testing during normal operating conditions without imposing operational restrictions.

chunks.text:
The generators shall withstand the following fault and abnormal conditions without any damage to the stator, rotor, windings and other parts of the generator.
Synchronizing shall be possible with the generator circuit breaker and 380kV circuit breaker.
Synchronising with the combined conditions based on maximum individual synchronising check tolerances of:
- ± 10 degrees phase displacement
- ± 0.7 percent slip
- ± 15 percent voltage
Fire detection and protection shall be provided. Generator shall be provided with required instruments to monitor temperature, oil pressure, vibration etc. These shall be wired out to junction boxes for field connection.
Gas turbine generators and related cooling systems shall be designed to maintain the temperature rise within insulation class B limits throughout the entire operational range and throughout the ranges of ambient temperatures.
The generator stator and rotor windings shall have class F insulation system.
Contractor shall optimise the Generators and as per SFR requirement shall provide suitable air cooled, closed air water cooled or hydrogen cooled.
The generator excitation system shall be complete with a fast response dual automatic voltage regulator, standby manual channel with auto follower and automatic transfer facilities. Monitoring and fault detecting devices with over and under excitation limiters, over-fluxing protection, power system stabiliser, reactive power control, field suppression equipment, dedicated instrument transformers and other required devices shall be provided to ensure a complete and reliable excitation system.
It shall be possible to continuously vary the generator terminal voltage under no load conditions between 50% and 110%. Facilities shall be included to control down to 0% of normal excitation for the purpose of commissioning.
The excitation power shall be derived either from a permanent magnet generator or from a power potential transformer connected to the terminals of the generator or from a SEE transformer which is fed from the 13.8kV MV Switchgear. The excitation system shall be brushless or static as appropriate. It is very important that the generators and the excitation system are suitable for grid connection.
Generator shall have AGC capability with all necessary hardware. Interface details between SEC and the Plant shall be finalized during detailed engineering stage.
Features of the excitation system shall include but not limited to:
- rotor current limiters
- rotor angle limiters
- under excitation alarm
- over excitation alarm
- volt-Hertz limiter and protection
- dual automatic channel
- manual channel
- reactive power control
- power system stabilizer
- field failure detection
- rotating diode monitoring where applicable
Generator compartments should be dust free. Contractor shall ensure that positive pressure in the generator terminal enclosure (GTE) is achieved if the generator is Hydrogen filled.
The design of the system shall be such that it is possible to carry out on-load replacement, and/or adjustment of the brushes. All necessary tools and equipment shall be provided to facilitate this work.

In particular, the following codes and standards shall be applicable:
- IEEE (ANSI) c37.013
- IEC standards (especially IEC 60056, 60694, 60298, 60129, 60044-1&2, 60099-4 and 60358)
The Gas Turbine shall incorporate a three-pole isolated phase breaker for main alternator on/off switching. These breakers shall be used for synchronising the generator to the grid and shall be designed for the necessary operating conditions and interrupting rate. The generator breaker switchgear panels shall be fitted with the following elements for each pole:
- SF6 alternator breaker in series with a motorized line breaker switch, with the required interlocking devices
- motorized earthing switches, one on the generator side and the other on the transformer side, with the required interlocking devices
- voltage transformers on the transformer side
- current transformer on the transformer side (if required)
- over-voltage discharger (auto-valves) on the transformer side
- protection capacitor on the transformer side
- devices and auxiliary circuits for signals and operations, both electrical and mechanical
Each generator breaker shall include a single-pole (isolated phase) sealed casing. The breaker casing shall be prepared for welding to the isolated phase busbar conductor casings. They shall incorporate viewports to allow visual checking of moving components (isolation switches), without having to open the casing.
The connection of generator breaker system active parts to those of the isolated phase busbars shall be made by means of flexible connection parts.
The breaker shall conduct the maximum generator output current and shall be able to withstand and break the short-circuit currents considering the reestablishment voltages under the most critical operating conditions.
Generator breaker failure protection within the tripping time set in the grid code including balance of equipment tripping shall be provided.
The breaker shall not be able to close if sufficient power is not available for opening. Two independent windings shall be available for opening. One winding is sufficient for closing. It shall be possible to open and close the breaker both locally and remotely.
Voltage transformers shall be installed on the transformer side (for synchronization and protection), with the power and precision required. These transformers shall be wired to the assembly control cabinet. The necessary resistance for protection against transformer resonance shall be fitted inside with open delta secondary. Each of the voltage outputs shall be protected with breaker switches.
To protect against over-voltages and increase the breaker voltage arc extinction effect, capacitor shall be installed on transformer side.
Both sides of the line switch-breaker assembly shall be fitted with blade-type earth switches to permit maintenance work. To this end, the necessary interlocks shall be fitted to both sides (transformer and generator). These connections shall not have current switch ON/OFF capability.

The design, construction, performance and testing of oil filled transformers shall be in accordance with IEC 60076. Transformer terminals and their provision will comply with IEC 60859.
Cooling shall be ONAN/ONAF/ODAF type for Generator Step-up Transformer (GSUT) and ONAN/ONAF type for Unit Auxiliary Transformer (UAT). The radiators may be mounted separate from the tank or mounted on the transformer tank.
Step-up transformer shall be equipped with on load tap changers. The other transformers shall be equipped with off load tap changers. The tap range, impedance and losses shall be selected to enable full output under normal conditions which allow for the highest and lowest system voltage operation and shall not be restricted over the specified ambient range.
All oil cooled transformers shall have the following as minimum:
- oil conservator
- oil level indication/alarm
- oil sampling device
- silica gel breather
- winding temperature/alarm/tripping
- pressure relief/alarm/tripping
- Buchholz gas and surge protection/tripping/alarm
- oil temperature indicator with alarm/trip contacts
Each transformer shall be fitted with a gas and surge actuated Buchholz relay of approved make and pattern, having alarm and tripping contacts which close simultaneously in response to both liquid surge and low oil level.
Approved facilities shall be provided for inspection, testing and maintenance access to the gas and oil-actuated relays and conservators associated with the transformers.
Transformers shall be located in suitable open concrete enclosures and including oil/water catchment sumps which discharge to the oily water separator drainage system.
All links contained within the transformer tank for earthing and other purposes shall be readily accessible and the links and their fixings shall be of the captive type.
Dry type transformers shall be located in transformer compartments/housings with a protection class of minimum IP23DW.

chunks.text:
Generator transformers shall be provided and shown on the single line diagrams. Generator transformers shall be connected to generator using isolated phase busducts. The generator transformer and the isolated phase busduct system shall be designed to transmit the maximum output from the corresponding unit without any limitation and under all ambient conditions.
The windings will be star in H.V, connected to earth directly, and delta in M.V. with a vectorial group of YNd1.
The generator transformer impedance shall be Minimum 14% (IEC basis).
Generator step up transformers shall be equipped with tap changers to be on load type. On load tap changer (OLTC) shall be provided as required by the Saudi Arabian Grid Code setting range shall be a minimum+/- 10 x 1.1% of rated voltage.
The OLTC shall be in conformity with IEC 60214 (or equivalent ANSI standard). OLTC shall have been type tested, and related type test certificates shall be supplied with the offer. Only designs which have been type tested in accordance with the relevant IEC standards will be accepted.
All equipment related to the OLTC shall be supplied by the original OLTC manufacturer. This is also applicable for tie-in resistors, if provided, as well as all related accessories. License products etc. are not acceptable for any equipment related to OLTC.
The OLTC shall withstand all kinds of through-fault currents without damage. All OLTC connected to uniformly insulated windings shall have at least same LI and AC voltage withstand levels as the related windings. The OLTC tank should be designed that the OLTC can be removed/replaced without removal of transformer windings/core and top cover of the main tank.
The motor drive, plus all auxiliary equipment for operation of the tap changer, shall be incorporated in a rigid control cabinet, protection class IP56 and shall be mounted onto the transformer tank in a convenient floor height. The driving gear shall be of the belt-type or equivalent dry-type gear. Oil filled driving gears are not acceptable. The electrical supply for the control of the cooling units and for motor drive of OLTC shall be provided by means of two independent feeders (load-break switches) installed in the control cabinet.
To cover the event of an electrical supply failure, automatic switchover from the first feeder to the second feeder is required.
Automatic transfer equipment shall include a time delay relay to prevent immediate transfer from normal to emergency source.
Step-Up Generator Transformer shall be provided with the following minimum electrical protections:
- restricted E/F protection (ANSI code 51TN)
- differential protection (ANSO code 87T)
- overcurrent protection (ANSI code 50/51)
- ground O/C protection (ANSI code 51G)
- overfluxing protection (external) ANSI 24

UAT shall be connected to the generator and step-up transformer through the isolated phase busduct system. UAT shall be sized to load the entire electrical loads for it's own unit normal operating allowing the biggest motor start-up and inside permissible voltage range, and during unit start up.
The windings will be delta in HV and star in MV, connected to earth by resistance, with a vectorial group of Dyn11. The HV winding will be provided of a manual tap changer with five positions (off-circuit tap changers, the tappings and range to be +/- 2 x 2.5% of the rated voltage.)
The Unit auxiliary transformers shall be designed for all the ambient conditions at site.
The UAT rated power and impedance should be justified with the electrical calculations.
UAT shall be provided with the following minimum electrical protections:
- differential protection (ANSO code 87T)
- overcurrent protection (ANSI code 50/51) at 18kV side
- ground O/C protection (ANSI code 51G)
- to protect IPB during generator start-up (breaker open), ground detector relay should be included (ANSI code 64) connected to open delta VT on GCB
All transformers to be equipped with the appropriate class of protection / metering CTs, as required.

The Contractor shall suitably size ML/LV transformers taking into account power requirements of the Plant.
Main MV/LV transformers should be sized to feed all the main LV switchboard (normal operation with bus tie closed and the other incomer open). MV/LV transformers shall be sized to load the entire electrical loads for it's own unit during normal operating allowing the start-up of the biggest motor and inside permissible voltage range.
Connection between MV/LV transformers and LV switchboards should be through LV copper power busbars.
The numbers and ratings of the various auxiliary transformers required around the plant are to be determined by the Contractor based on his load estimates for each service or building.
The LV transformers have to be designed as oil immersed, threephase power transformer for outdoor installation. The dry type can be accepted only for indoor installations; however as an exception only for GTG package, outdoor dry type cast coil rated transformers supplied by GTG OEM can be accepted subject to satisfying Exhibit B, Part 1 requirements.
The transformer neutral point on the low voltage winding shall be solidly grounded.
These transformers will step down from the MV to LV and be fitted with off-circuit tap changing facilities of range ±2 x 2.5% steps

Each resistor shall be enclosed in a naturally ventilated protected weatherproof cubicle located outdoors alongside their respective equipment.

chunks.text:
All main switchboards, MCC, relay panels, control equipment etc. shall be provided with redundant power supplies for control and alarm purposes.
A two position (Local/Remote i.e. Switchgear/CCR) selector switch shall be provided at the switchgear for all switchgear incomer, bussection, feeder and interconnector circuits respectively for switchgear emergency control and isolated testing/CCR remote control.
Check-synchronising facilities shall be included for the main incomers of the MV systems (at least two different sources). MV transfer between UAT incomer and start-up incomer shall be high speed transfer with short parallel.
The LV switchgear system main incomers, interconnectors and bus-section circuits shall exclude check-synchronising facilities but shall be electrically interlocked to prevent the paralleling of two incoming supplies to a switchboard.
Circuit breakers supplied shall be identical to those used for the type tests for which certificates are submitted.
MV switchgear and all main LV switchgear shall be of withdrawable type. Fault levels and thermal withstand time for MV and LV switchboards shall be in accordance with the technical requirements of the appropriate standards.

chunks.text:
MVswitchgear and control gear shall comply with IEC 60298 and shall be metal-clad.
MV circuit breakers shall comply with IEC 60056 and shall be of withdrawable three pole circuit breakers, using vacuum interrupters type.
The MV switchgears shall be designed for a nominal voltage of 13.8 kV, to be internal arc certified IAC=AFRL according IEC 62271-200 and to withstand a short-circuit current of minimum 10% higher than required by calculations for a duration of three (3) seconds.
The mechanical protection class for all MV switchgears shall be minimum IP41.
Where operation of a switching device can give rise to surge voltages which would be detrimental to the insulation of the equipment controlled, surge suppressers shall be installed in the switchgear to control these voltages to a safe level.

chunks.text:
LV circuit breakers shall comply with IEC 60947-2. Withdrawable air circuit breakers or moulded case circuit breakers shall be used, unless otherwise approved.
LV switchgear and control gear shall comply with the relevant IEC and/or NEMA standards. It shall be metal-clad and generally of multicubicle of Form 4 construction and Form 3b for MCC cubicles.
Panels for different feeder circuits shall be appropriately equipped with control, metering, alarm and protection devices based on Good Industry Practices and current technology.
The construction shall be such that the various components of the switchgear are segregated electrically from each other.
Moulded case circuit-breakers and miniature circuit-breakers may be used if they are properly selected to withstand the maximum specified short-circuit current level and evidence of acceptable performance is provided by the Contractor.
LV contactors used as motor starters shall be of the air-break type with arc shields and to class AC3/AC4 according to IEC standards. It is acceptable for the GTG OEM only to offer 480V AC MCC built according to NEMA standards provided IEC standard requirements are satisfied under NEMA standards.
An earthing bar with a minimum cross-section of 240mm2 shall run the full length of the switchboards. The Contractor will connect to this bar all metallic parts not forming part of the live circuits and all CT points to be earthed. Chassis of circuit-breakers shall be directly connected to the earthing bar.
Every low voltage switchboards shall have spare columns with equipped reserve (two breakers) and empty space (for future necessities a 20% free space of reserve must be included)
