chunks.text:
Phase isolated busducts with aluminium enclosures shall be used for the connections between the turbine generators and generator transformer and for unit auxiliary transformer connection. These busducts shall be of pressurised with instrument air (clean and dry) to exclude dust and moisture. For connections between MV switchgear and MV/LV transformers cables shall be provided.
The outer enclosure shall be of the self-supporting type and kept at a slight overpressure to avoid ingress of humidity. The enclosure shall be earthed and fitted with drain plugs at the lowest points.
The generated heat shall be dissipated by natural radiation and convection. No forced air-cooling shall be provided.
The allowable temperatures under full-load operation at site conditions shall be as per the relevant IEC/ANSI Standards
Generator and MV (as applicable) busducts shall be pressurised with instrument air (cleaned and dried air), anti-condensation heaters are not necessary.
Outdoor section of busducts shall be provided with sun shades. Complete steel support structures shall be provided. Busducts shall be terminated using flexible busbars and rubber/neoprene bellows.

chunks.text:
The Contractor will be responsible for the design, manufacture, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of control, monitoring and protection systems associated with his electrical installation. Control and alarm facilities for the power plant electrical MV, LV and DC systems shall be provided.
The scope of supply shall comprise all necessary control, protection, monitoring and supervisory equipment, cabling and wiring, regardless of whether it is specifically mentioned or not, for safe and efficient operation of the Plant. The control and monitoring of the electrical system and other associated common systems shall include at least the following:
- control and monitoring of MV system via ECMS or Plant DCMS and Digital fault Monitoring System
- control and monitoring of auxiliary power distribution (LV, DC, UPS) via Plant DCMS and Digital fault Monitoring System
- energy meters via Plant DCMS
- alarm facia/windows to be provided on Electrical Panels and Fire Protection Panels
- auxiliary and marshalling cubicles via plant DCMS
MV and LV AC electrical systems (excluding LV sub-distribution systems) shall be monitored and controlled from the CCR including for all transformers, switchgear incomers, bus-section, feeders and interconnector circuits via the plant DCMS. Manual and auto synchronising facilities shall be included for these circuits. The voltage of each switchboard and single phase current of all main circuits (incomers, bus-sections, feeders and interconnectors) shall be displayed locally at each switchgear, and for motors of 55kW and above repeated in the central control room via the plant DCMS.
Motor circuits shall normally be controlled and monitored from the central control room via the plant DCMS, except for station minor plant needing only local control. For motors of 50kW and above the single phase current of each motor circuit shall be displayed locally at each switchboard.
Alternative locations of control of switchgear and motors shall be at the switchgear (under Permit to Work for operation or testing) or plant (for operation or maintenance).
LV sub-distribution systems and the DC systems shall be locally controlled only, but alarms shall be transmitted to the central control room via the plant DCMS.
The switchgear shall include all related circuit prominent coloured LED type status and alarm lamps. The associated protection relays shall also include LED status/alarm indicators or flags.
Communication between the plant DCMS and ESF including the switchyard signal shall be done via a SEC/SA approved method such as a serial link using dual redundant MODBUS protocol for monitoring major switchyard and electrical signals from plant DCMS.
Sequence of Events (SOE), GT and ST operation signals shall be through hardwire interface to the DCMS.

All distribution boards shall comply with IEC 60439, IEC 60937 and other related IEC standards and, for the enclosure, comply with IEC 60529. They shall be of Form 2 construction as a minimum.
All distribution boards situated outside shall be of the weatherproof enclosure type IPW54. They shall be capable of withstanding the associated fault current until the related protection operates.
The AC sub-distribution boards shall be either single phase or three phase and neutral types, and the DC sub-distribution boards shall be of the two-pole type. All distribution boards shall be rated for the full load current of the incoming supply and equipped with an incomer moulded case circuit breaker (MCCB) isolator and with removable miniature circuit breakers (MCBs) to provide overcurrent protection to each sub circuit.

chunks.text:
All motors shall be designed and manufactured in accordance with IEC 60034 and other related internationally recognised standards. Motors in hazardous areas shall be suitably certified.
NEMA is accepted, but Contractor shall ensure:
- the starting current of MV motors does not exceed 5.5 times the rated current
- the starting current for LV motors does not exceed 6 times the rated current
- and prove during detailed engineering that there is no disturbance to the electrical system due to LV motors start ups
Motors of the same type must be fully interchangeable and shall comply as far as applicable with IEC standard motor dimensions. AC motors shall be of the squirrel cage induction type provided with either deep slots or double squirrel cages.
All motors shall normally be of the totally enclosed fan-cooled type or water-cooled type, of protection class IPW54 according to IEC recommendations 60034 and 60529. Where motors are installed outdoors a weatherproof design (minimum IPW55) shall be chosen. Motorised valves shall be to protection class IP65.
Motors shall have Class F insulation but the temperature rise shall not exceed Class B.
DC motors and starters shall be designed for high reliability with direct-on-line starting using a permanently connected series resistance in the armature. Service voltage for GTG OEM DC motors can be 125 VDC.
Emergency stop buttons of the stay-put key-reset red button mushroom head type shall be provided adjacent to all MV motors and all lubricating oil pumps. These buttons shall directly trip the motors, prevent a start until reset and alarm their operation to the central control room. The buttons shall all use a common reset key. This requirement may be relaxed for certain essential loads in the GT package as stopping of lube oil to the generator and turbine will severely damage those units.
The service voltages of the motors will be:
- MV, 3-phase AC, 60Hz, for motors above about 200kW
- 460V, 3-phase AC, 60Hz, for motors below and including about 200kW Calculations of the voltage drop at start-up shall be made for each motor to additionally verify the capability to cross line starting
The rating of each motor shall be adequate to meet the requirements of its associated load, without infringing upon the service factor as per NEMA and/or ANSI standards
Motors shall be capable of operating continuously under rated output conditions at any frequency between 58 and 62 Hz and/or with any voltage deviation between 90% and 110% of the nominal voltage. A transient overvoltage of 130% of the nominal voltage shall also be sustainable. Further, the motors shall be capable of delivering the maximum torque as required by the driven machine when running at 80% nominal voltage for a period of 5 seconds without damaging, overheating or slipping.

chunks.text:
The pullout torque for continuously loaded motors shall be at least 160% of the rated motor torque and for intermittently loaded motors 200% of the rated motor torque.
Fixed speed AC motors shall be designed for direct on-line starting.
The number of starts in one hour for all motors shall be in compliance with relevant standards and shall be determined during the detailed design stage. At the end of the determined number of starts the temperature of the insulated windings shall not exceed the maximum permitted temperature for class B insulation, and the cage windings shall not suffer damaging temperature rise.
Each MV motor shall be capable of enduring two successive starts with the motor initially at operating temperature and the temperature of the winding at the end of start shall not exceed the Class B limit. Each LV motor shall be capable of withstanding three successive starts under the same conditions or once every twenty minutes without damaging temperature rise.
For the start-up of electrical drives of chillers should not perturb the electrical system, therefore. Contractor shall stagger and optimise the chiller start up process and its configuration adequately accordingly.

The Contractor shall suitably size DC and UPS systems taking into account power requirements of the Plant. The Contractor will supply UPS and DC systems to meet all the site DC requirements consisting of at least two (2) x 100% battery chargers, one (1) x 100% Nickel cadmium batteries (use of lead acid batteries (VRLA type) instead of Ni-Cd batteries is subject to approval during design stage), DC distribution panels, two (2) x 100% AC Inverters, and AC Distribution panel for UPS consisting of two coupled bus sections. The 120V Safe AC system shall consist of 2 x 100% invertors each equipped with a static by pass switch and a related safe AC distribution consisting of two coupled bus sections. UPS power for the gas turbines shall be provided from the Plant UPS. AC un-interruptible power supplies are to be provided for equipment requiring continuity of supply or equipment that need supply during emergency operation, when the normal power supply is lost. The rated capacity of the batteries shall be adequate for discharge duration of 1 hour for the emergency consumers. The UPS system shall be also be provided with a bypass static switch, autonomy will be 1 hour.
DC nominal voltage level should be 125VDC and UPS nominal voltage level should be 120V. The chargers shall be designed for operation from the 480V, 60Hz supply. Each charger shall be rated to ensure simultaneously battery charging and the supply of the full DC load. Under normal operating conditions, charging of a fully discharged battery will take a maximum of 10 hours. Each battery charger shall be capable of fully charging the battery on initial installation. Battery chargers shall have facilities for on-line maintenance.

The Contractor shall undertake all relevant design and engineering of the cable systems for equipment in his supply, and shall prepare the cable connection schematic diagrams, terminal diagrams, cable lists, cable schedule and the cable route plans. All cables shall comply with the relevant IEC standards. It is acceptable for the GTG OEM only to offer cables according to NEMA standards provided IEC standard requirements are satisfied under NEMA standards.
All power cables shall be of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) and shall be capable of continuous operation at the highest system voltage specified with a maximum conductor temperature of 90°C, under rated conditions and a maximum temperature under fault conditions of not more than 250°C. Use of PVC cables for LV duty shall be subject to approval.
All power and control cables capacity sizing shall be in accordance with the temperatures given in Exhibit B, Part 1. Cables installed on cable trays that may be exposed to sunlight during operation shall have ultra violet safe insulation.
Control cables shall be multicore, PVC insulated types withstanding without deterioration the conditions prevailing at each installation location. Cables for analogue signals shall have a common screen of metal tape, cores shall be twisted by pairs, for process computers, each pair shall be separately screened. Control and instrumentation cables shall be armoured for outdoor applications and all cables shall be shielded, with a minimum conductor section of 0.5mm2, alternatively un-armoured cables for control and instrumentation is acceptable for outdoor application if laid on conduit, trench, duct bank, tray, ladder (i.e., with suitable protection). Cables above ground shall be laid in trays or on ladder racks or conduits and shall be segregated from power cables in accordance with International standards. Cables shall be labelled and conductors shall be identified at terminations by ferrule number or suitable proprietary method.
Every cable end of MV/LV power cables shall be sealed and protected in an approved manner consistent with the voltage levels, cable type, and place of installation.
"Plug-in" cables terminations (if supplied) shall be in accordance with the characteristics of the MV switchgears.
MV and LV cables are generally to be laid in cable trays (inside buildings) and in cable trenches and/or cable trays (outside buildings). Any cables direct buried shall be armoured.
Cables running inside buildings or concrete trenches shall be laid on trays. The trays shall be of adequate strength and size to carry in one layer, the weight, number and configuration required for each tray plus additional cables, not less than 25% by weight and dimensions, in excess of those installed.
Segregation of the various services and voltage levels shall be achieved by use of separate trays and marshalling boxes (when required) separate for each voltage grade of cable used. .

For the data highway communication link, spatially separated routing with the cables running in galvanised steel conduits of approved type shall be supplied and installed.
All power, control and instrumentation cables shall be Flame Retardant Low Smoke type and shall comply with IEC-332 Part 3.
Wherever practical, all electrical/instrumentation circuit shall be routed above grade via a cable tray. For the outdoor areas, underground duct banks and/or cable trenches shall be used where exposed raceway is not practical.
Additionally, Contractor shall consider the required MV and LV cables for the power plants interconnection, all the necessary works will be in Contractor scope (required cable trenches, cable supporting systems etc.) to carry out the interconnections.

Cable trays shall be used to support cables.
Heavy duty, hot dipped galvanized and epoxy coated, ladder type with channel side cable trays shall be used for outdoor cable installations.
Within Indoor areas, tray covers shall be used where physical protection of cable is needed. For outdoor installation, tray covers will be used on the highest level to protect cables from direct sunlight and on other levels to protect from water etc. as required.
Cable tray shall be segregated, top to down, as follows:
- medium voltage power circuits
- low voltage AC power circuits not over than 600VAC
- 230VAC/125VDC control circuits
- analogue low level signal or other analogue signal and 24VDC signal from instrumentation/other devices
- fibre optical cable (as long as it is proven by Contractor that no interference will occur providing signal cable and fibre optical cable in same trays are acceptable)
Low level control cable may be run in the low voltage power cable tray or 230 VAC/125VDC control cable tray when separated by a continuous barrier to prevent mixing.
In a vertical configuration, low voltage power cable trays shall be located below medium voltage power cable trays; control cable trays shall be located below low voltage power cable trays; instrumentation cable trays will be located below control cable trays.
In general, average maintained minimum vertical spacing for cable tray shall be 300mm, measured from the bottom of the upper tray to the top of the lower tray.
At least a 200mm clearance shall be maintained between the top of a tray and beams, piping, etc., to facilitate installation of cables in tray.
The cross member or lung of cable tray shall be spaced maximum of 300mm on centers.
Complete support system for the cable trays including all hangers, braces, brackets, inserts, anchors, fabricated structures, hardware and incidental materials utilizing unistrut type or equal supports and hangers wherever possible shall be provided.

In general, hot dipped galvanized, rigid steel conduit shall be used for exposed conduit. The minimum size for power and lighting circuits shall be 22mm, and for communication and other circuits will be 16mm.
The conduit shall be securely fastened to the cable tray with clamp-type fasteners, and the end of the conduit shall be equipped with an insulated conduit grounding bushing.
Solid insulated bushings shall be provided for all conduit 42mm and smaller when not terminated in a box.
For rigid conduits enter sheet metal enclosure, threaded hubs shall be used.
When conduit passes through concrete slabs, galvanized steel pipe which extended 150mm above the surface of slab shall be provided. Conduit should be made of galvanized steel and should extend 150mm when passing through concrete. Contractor can use PVC to cross concrete slabs, and galvanized steel pipe can pass through this PVC pipe. It is mandatory to install galvanized steel pipes.
Complete galvanized support system including all hangers, brackets, inserts, anchors, steel structures and hardware shall be provided.
Unistrut type or equal conduit hangers and supports shall be used.
Conduit body shall not be used for grounding purposes.
label: text

chunks.text:
Liquid tight flexible conduit will be used between motor terminal boxes, or other equipment subject to vibration and/or mechanical adjustment and the rigid conduit systems.
Liquid tight flexible conduit to be used will be a type fabricated of galvanized steel conduit flexible tubing with a synthetic jacket extruded over the tubing.
The length of this conduit is not less than twelve times the conduit diameter (trade size), minimum 300mm.
label: text

chunks.text:
In general, all underground raceway shall use heavy wall high density polyvinyl chloride conduit or hot-dipped galvanized steel conduit encased in concrete.
Where practicable, duct size shall be standardized and minimum may be 75mm .
Duct banks will be separated and supported by using nonmagnetic materials to keep 75mm minimum spacing between the outer surfaces of the conduits.
All duct banks shall be provided with a reinforced concrete encasement. Minimum of 75mm concrete covering on sides, top and bottom will be provided. No waterproofing of the encasement will be considered.
The top of the duct bank encasement shall keep a minimum distance of 300mm below finished grade where applicable.
Ground wire that follows routes of duct banks may be laid directly on top or side of duct bank encasements.
Manholes shall be provided in underground duct runs so that duct lengths will not exceed those which will develop pulling tensions greater than allowed by the cable manufacturers. The maximum length of a duct bank between manholes (pulling points) will not exceed 90m. Pulling eyes will be installed on walls of manholes.
Manholes will be of the precast or cast in situ type.
Floors of manholes shall have slope to a sump in one corner or a drain pipe to the drainage system.
Where a duct bank turns upward for continuation above grade, the last 2.4m (8 feet) of the underground portion may include a transition to heavy-wall hot-dipped galvanized steel conduit and terminate approximately 150 mm above grade. If a bend exceeds 2.7m then manholes shall be provided.

The scope of supply shall include all required copper conductors, and earth rods, connecting material, and all attachment material to make up a complete, safe and reliable system. All electrical equipment such as motors, transformers, switchboards, control boards, relay and auxiliary relay boards, and all other subsidiary electrical equipment, as well as all metal parts of the civil structure or the mechanical equipment which might be subject to earth fault currents shall be connected to this network.
The Contractor will provide a potential gradient control system for the switchgear rooms and all such locations where dangerous surface voltage gradients may occur.
Each building roof or civil structure protective cover shall be provided with a lightning protection system composed of roof collectors and down conductors of adequate dimensions and spacing connected to the earthing electrodes.
Metallic structures or equipment housings located on the roofs of buildings shall be connected to the lightning protection conductors, with the equipment earthed via the earthing network.
The lightning protection system shall be bonded to the Plant's earthing system and shall be according to the applicable NFPA and/or other internationally recognised standards.
It shall be the responsibility of Contractor to ensure that proper and safe earthing is provided for the plant; Earthing calculations should be carried out (dissipate electric currents into the earth and no danger to electrical shock - touch and step voltages values).

All the processes shall be completely automated and they shall be controlled from the main control room.
The control and automation systems of the Plant shall be designed and realised using a proven, state of the art modern control system and computer technology as specified in Exhibit B, Part 1 and shall also fulfil the following requirements:
- the plant can be run efficiently and safely
- the plant shall be operated in the most cost effective manner
- the Plant operation is to be based on Central Control Room (CCR) principle
- the Plant shall be designed with a view to high reliability and availability with a minimum of operator intervention being necessary during the normal operation
- all the normal operations including start-ups and shutdown (exception can be given after long term outages) of single GT/HRSGs or whole Plant shall be performed by the operator in the permanently manned CCR without any dedicated field operations
The major Plant components such as gas turbines can have their own control systems with interfaces to the Distributed Control and Monitoring system (DCMS) so that it is fully transparent to the operator i.e. operator interface is identical irrespective of actual control system used. However, number of control systems interfaced to the main DCMS (subcontrol systems) is to be kept at a minimum. All these sub-systems shall be operated through the main DCMS.
There may be separate local control rooms where appropriate sub-processes can be monitored as may be necessary time-to-time for maintenance purposes but not permanently and all necessary data and information and control shall be managed from the Central Control Room (CCR).
The Plant automation and operating concept shall be designed to enable fully automated normal operation (including start-ups and shutdowns) with two operators carrying out all control and monitoring tasks in normal operation in the main control room.

The Plant shall be controlled and monitored via a Distributed Control System (DCMS). The usage of separate programmable logic controllers (PLCs) or other separate and specialised control systems shall be minimized. Typical and acceptable reasons for a specialised control system can be high speed of response as typically required at gas turbine and steam turbine control, or special safety requirements, which may require a separate safety-related system (e.g. for boiler protection).
If specialised separate control systems or pre-packaged PLCs are supplied, they shall be monitored and operated solely by the operator workstations of the DCMS. The interface to the DCMS shall be either of conventional hardwired type (small amount of signals) or of a well-known communication data link type (e.g. Modbus or Profibus DP).
The cabinets containing the control system electronics shall be placed in a room in the control building. Electronic cabinets dedicated to signal acquisition (remote I/O- cabinets) could be installed at field. For all the equipment not installed in air-conditioned environment, provisions shall be made for an adequate protection degree (IP 55 minimum).

Control and monitoring of main processes shall be carried out with the Distributed Control and System (DCMS). The DCMS shall take care of all automation functions, such as:
- open loop drive controls, group controls, and sequence controls
- equipment protection of individual drives (pumps, valves, etc.)
- closed loop drive controls and co-ordinating controls
- man-machine interface as process displays and trend reports
- alarm annunciation
- self-diagnostics
- process interface and power supply for field equipment, signal conditioning
- interface to external systems as PLCs, computers, local area network (LAN), etc
- back-up functions
- engineering functions
The availability and reliability level of the DCMS shall not compromise the one of the Plant. For this purpose, adequate redundancy of processors, communication buses, supply devices, etc. shall be used. The following requirements shall be taken into consideration by the Contractor:
- all processes can be controlled and monitored via any operator terminal (display capacity shall be high enough)
- however, each operator terminal can be authorised to carry out the control and monitoring only of the specified processes (authorisation shall be possible)

- a single failure of a redundant component does not cause a spurious intervention of the protection system nor make it ineffective and, in any case, the failure of a single component does not cause the protection system to become ineffective
- when redundant field sensors are foreseen (duplicated or triplicate), each of them shall be acquired by an input card different from that of the other redundant sensors

All Plant equipment and system controls shall be achieved by Distributed Control System (DCMS) stations, local control systems which interface with DCMS, stand-alone control systems and hardwired circuits. With respect to local control systems associated to GTs and ST, the HMI station enabling a local control (e.g. screens in the PCC) will not be available after the Commercial Operation Date.
The system shall enable the following fundamental functions:
- acquisition, filtering, validation and conversion of both digital and analog input values originating from the process
- processing of all input values using:
- -sequence control performing succession of logic operations depending on previous orders and presence of criteria
- -combinatory (or interlocking) control that combines authorization criteria for sending orders that switch on/off one or several equipment, that realizes security actions and that generates the necessary alarms
- -analog control (open and closed loop) that keeps the process parameters at preset values (that are functions of the load of the Plant within the limits contractually foreseen)
- creating the output information for digital (on/off) or modulating actuators;
- working out of supervision information (including but not limited to status indications, alarms) for control room operators and for maintenance, planning or statistics
The automation stations (and other control stations) shall be connected to a number of operating stations in the Central Control Room (CCR) by data buses. Data handling systems such as archiving and interfaces with other systems shall also be connected to the system.
Control/supervision units receive data from their relevant packages control systems to perform remote control and/or monitoring of those packages. This includes sets of images, alarms and hardware buttons.
A redundant OPC server with DA and HDA protocols and the necessary license to provide access to all and every data available in the DCMS system shall be part of the scope of supply. The data access of the OPC-clients to the OPC-server is limited and licensed for up to 5000 signals.
The good working of the OPC server shall be demonstrated with an OPC client which shall also be part of the scope of supply.

The DCMS is operating on a 24 hours a day basis. Verifications, checking and maintenance operation may only happen during the scheduled partial outages of the Plant (while maintenance is performed the system will still be operational in degraded mode). Beyond the outage periods no preventive maintenance shall be required.
Repairing is to be performed during operation of the Plant and shall consist only in module replacement (with minimum needs in wiring disconnection).
After detection and localization of a faulty module maintenance may be performed without disturbance on overall operation of the system.
Critical sensors will be redundant or connected in a 3 out of 3 manner to individual I/O's: only loss of both sensors or both I/O's would lead to shut down of controlled system. Critical cards ( communication cards, power supply cards or devices, ..) shall be fully redundant. Contractor shall describe the principles of the segregation of redundant modules/devices to avoid any common mode fault.
The period between two successive maintenance actions (checks, controls and maintenance) cannot be shorter than 24 months.

The operator shall be kept alerted on the status of field signal non-reliability (invalid measurements or non-consistent contacts).
In case of double or triple measurements, information shall also be obtained when an excessive deviation is detected between measurements.
The management of the measures dedicated to control functions is proposed to follow the criteria listed below:
- in case of an invalidity of a single measurement (signal out of scale), information shall be given to the operator and in case the measurement is connected to a control loop, the loop shall be switched into manual mode
- in case of invalidity of one of the double measurement, the valid measurement shall remain used for the control (which remains in automatic) and an information to the operator shall given
- moreover, for double measurements, the deviation between the two channels shall be monitored and when the same exceeds the tolerance limit (that could be calibrated), after an appropriate time, an alarm shall be given to the control room and the concerned control loop shall be switched to manual
- in case deviation existing among the three measurements, taken two by two, shall be monitored. Whenever the detected deviation exceeds the tolerance limit (that could be calibrated), after an appropriate timing, the invalidity of the measurement channel deviation from the remaining two shall be declared. This shall automatically select the calculation of the mean on the two valid channels left (which shall be treated as double measure) and shall originate an alarm signal and the display of comparisons exceeding the limit set
- in case of double or triple measurements any measurement(s) could be manually excluded

- the alarm displaying on the monitor shall be complete with all the indications useful for the acknowledgement of the alarm

The following requirements shall be taken into consideration by the Contractor.
The Safety Related System (SRS) shall be an emergency shutdown system that shuts down part of the Plant whenever the safety limits have been exceeded. The SRS shall include all the sensors, logic, and final elements needed for the safety function.
The SRS is required for the gas turbines, steam turbines, HRSG and the fuel systems.
The SRS system shall fulfil the requirements of IEC 61508 or equivalent:
- the SRS shall be independent from the DCMS. A fault at DCMS side may not affect the functions of safety system
- the SRS system shall be fault tolerant so that no single fault inside the SRS will cause a loss of a safety function
- the SRS shall be redundant. A single fault inside the SRS system may not cause a spurious trip of the plant/unit
- the SRS shall have a certificate that it fulfils the integrity level 3 of the IEC 61508 or equivalent. The requirements of the certification body shall be followed
- the safety functions and the safety integrity functions shall be allocated to each SRS system based on risk analyse of the process
- the major property damage shall be protected using SIL level 2 (IEC 61508). In case there is a risk of losing several human lives, the SIL level shall be 3
- response time of the logic controller: the maximum allowed response time for the safety-related functions of the logic controller is proposed to be 500 ms, that is 50 % of the proposed response time of 1 s
- in case the risk analyses indicates faster than 1 s response time, the SRS system shall fulfil that requirement

The critical protection functions shall be realized using multichannel techniques with the 2 out of 3 redundancy principle.
Multichannel technique is provided for "Fail-safe" protection which will be limited to such systems which jeopardize the safety of persons. Such features are limited to fail safe systems of GTs, STs and HRSGs. All important, fail safe relevant measurements will be triplicated (exception: absolute bearing casing vibration, external binary trip signals). The fail-safe protection system itself shall be executed as a 1 out of 2 controller redundancy.
The system works preferably according to principle of current switch-on to actuate and de-energize to trip.
A single failure shall not prevent a protection to be activated.
A single fault shall not trigger a protection if not required.
Measures shall be taken so as to ensure that orders of such critical functions are duly sent to the actuators, in particular but not restricted:
- power distribution will be sufficiently subdivided in order to prevent a fault from having repercussions on different functions: complete selectivity of protection will be achieved
- binary and analog outputs are neutralized during initialization and start-up of the CPU's
- each signal used for critical functions shall be validated by continuous monitoring of its value and/or the variation thereof in relation to other values/signals: associated digital information is made available for any further functional processing
- interruption of a single external AC power supply won't impair operation of the DCMS (UPS power for the DCMS is redundancy provided)

A consistent control and instrumentation philosophy shall apply throughout the plant and shall be implemented in terms of a range of equipment exhibiting a minimum diversity of type and manufacture. The objective shall be to standardize all measurement and control equipment throughout the plant (except for the GT/ST/HRSG/Package suppliers) in order to rationalize operation, maintenance and reduce spares holding.
Generally equipment shall be supplied from one composite range of measurement and control equipment as marked by a reputable manufacturer of international standing and shall have operational use on similar projects. The equipment shall be of modern compact design incorporating the latest developments in proven technology.
Minimum protection degree IP 54 shall be provided for equipment in normal environment. IP 65 shall be provided in dusty environments, for open buildings, for outdoor installation and field installed instrument or explosion proof equipment following Eexd or Eexi when required.
All components shall be designed for the local ambient conditions. Equipment shall be designed to withstand the worst site conditions without deterioration in its functionality beyond the typical wear and tear. Field equipment shall have an appropriate degree of environmental protection.
The instruments shall not be shared between control/monitoring systems and plant protection systems. In cases where this is not practical or there is sufficient technical justification (e.g. measurement redundancy) in doing so, a shared arrangement may be used subject to the approval of the Owner/Engineer. In this case, the field signals shall be connected directly to the plant protection system where the pre-processing of the signals shall be carried out, thus avoiding the possible dependence of the protection system on the related control system for its inputs.
Analogue signals shall be standardized at 4-20 mA in the field. Direct current plant status and alarm signals shall be standardized on a DC voltage level between 22 to 50V. Instruments without separate power supply shall be chosen (excepted where impossible). Power supplies for current loops shall have a dedicated fused link for protection and isolation.
Two wire programmable smart type transmitters (e.g. HART) shall be provided. Transmitters used for control and monitoring may be hardwired to the DCMS I/O system or connected by a proven 'Fieldbus' communication system. However, transmitters used in functional safety systems shall be hardwired.
All transmitters shall have local indication of the measured value either built-in or equipped with separately mounted local indicator. Transmitters (except temperature transmitter and radar level transmitters) shall be provided with test connections and instrument isolating valve manifolds where appropriate.
Instrument ranges shall be chosen such that the nominal operating point lies between 60% and 75% of the measurement span.
Transmitters shall be used wherever possible instead of switches however, switches may be used with the approval of the Owner/Engineer in cases where their use can be technically justified. Switches shall be of the heavy-duty type with double pole changeover contacts. Mercury switches shall not be used. Transmitters and switches used for functional safety shall have traceable and appropriate SIL ratings.

Each tapping point shall be dedicated to only a single instrument.
All measuring devices shall be provided with instrument isolating valves, vent/test valves and instrument manifolds where appropriate to enable them to be disconnected from the connecting pipe work without having to disconnect or drain the pipe work. Instrument impulse lines shall use compression type tube fittings.
The impulse lines shall be arranged so as to avoid any gas bubbles entering piping for liquids (and liquids entering gas piping). Unless otherwise specified on the erection drawings, the slope of the impulse lines from the process shall be at least 10% of length (to the connection point when the instrument is placed higher than this connection point, and to the instrument when the instrument is placed lower than the connection point);
If necessary, pneumatic piping shall be laid in perforated cable trays supported at least every 0.6m.
All instruments and their piping shall be fixed in a way that prevents vibrations being generated or transmitted and the Contractor shall be taken into the fact that process piping and equipment may be subject to expansion or contraction.

Irrespective of the specific function that a control valve performs in the control scheme, i.e. modulating, inching or on/off, all control valves shall have a local control facility and local indication of the actual position of the valve. The normal operating mode shall be 'remote' from the CCR via the DCMS, the selection of which shall be local to the valve and transmitted to the DCMS.
Control valves shall be supplied with suitable actuators matched to the operational and environmental requirements of the plant. In general, pneumatic actuated control valves shall be used for modulating duties. However, motorised control valves or hydraulic valves may also be used in specific control loops with the approval of the Owner. Control valves for inching duty shall be of the motorised type. On/off control valves may be motorised or pneumatically actuated with a solenoid pilot valve.
In general, all control valves shall have end-position detection by limit switches and indication in the CCR. Modulating and inching valves shall have transmitters or LVDT's to indicate the valve position in the CCR, the measurement of which shall be taken directly from the actual valve position.
label: text

chunks.text:
Motorized valves shall consist of self-contained actuator units with motor, gearbox, electric/electronic controls, limit/torque switches and all auxiliary devices installed in the actuator housing. A lockable local/remote selector switch with open/close controls shall be located on the actuator. Only for the Gas Turbine package, for safety reasons if some valves are not lockable it is acceptable. The actuator shall be provided with a hand wheel for operation of the valve in an emergency. Only for the Gas Turbine package, for safety reasons if some actuators do not have hand wheels it is acceptable. The operation of the hand wheel shall disengage the actuating motor to prevent damage.
Each end of the actuator travel shall be fitted with suitable limit and torque switches and correctly set up for preventing over travel and consequential damage to the actuator. The stopping of the operating mechanism on limit or torque switch shall be determined based on the specific application for which the valve is used. Adjustment of maximum torque shall be performed at works. Torque shall be adjustable from 80 to 115% of rated torque value demanded by valve;
Semiconductor power-electronic switches rather than contactors shall be used in the actuator for switching the motor supply.
Motorized valves shall be equipped with Anti-condensate heater.
Control and supervision signals to DCMS or Control System:
- OPEN and CLOSE control
- open and Closed position in feedback
- open and close torque faults
- motor in 'local/remote control'
- motor General 'fault'

An electro-pneumatic converter shall generate a 0.2 to 1.0 bar pneumatic signal from a 4 to 20 mA electric signal for use by the actuator positioner for modulating duties. On/off applications shall make use of a solenoid pilot valve with a suitable operating voltage to minimise volt drop on the connecting cable.
Control valve actuators shall be designed to drive the valve to a safe position from the process view point on failure of signal and/or air supply. For each valve application, due consideration shall be given to whether the safe state is open, closed or for the valve to remain in the last position prior to loss of control ('stay put' design). The fail-safe position for all pneumatic control valves shall be advised during the detailed design of the system.
Volume boosters shall be provided between the actuator and the control valve where necessary, e.g. on fast-acting loops.
All positioners and electro/pneumatic converters shall be furnished with pressure gauges for air supply, signal input and control air output.

The interface between the MCC and the control system shall be standardised. This shall include on/off command inputs to the MCC and on/off/unavailable/fault feedback signals to the DCMS. The command inputs to the MCC shall be electrically rated to allow a direct connection (i.e. without the use of external interposing relays) with the DCMS binary output module.

The use of a VSD shall be based on a cost-benefit analysis in terms of energy saving and/or the need for achieving the required level of modulating control performance of the process.
The signals exchanged between the VSD and the DCMS shall be categorised into critical and non-critical. The critical signals (e.g. speed reference, speed feedback, drive trip command, drive fault, drive common alarm) shall be hardwired. The non-critical signals (e.g. internal drive status and warning signals) shall be communicated to the DCMS via a serial data communication link using a standard fieldbus communication protocol.
Segregation in terms of cabling and DCMS I/O modules shall be provided for duty/standby pumps/fans.

I&C cabling shall use multi-pair cables with screens, multi-core cables and optical fibre cables as appropriate. The cables shall be of the rodent proof, flame resistant and fire retardant type. The multi-pair/multi-core cables shall be made up of copper conductors of not less than 1 mm2 cross-section except for those associated with interposing relay cubicles and power supplies where higher conductor cross-section shall be chosen based on volt drop considerations. I&C cables of less than 1 mm2 cross-section shall be subject to approval by the Owner/Engineer.
There shall be 20% spare conductors as a minimum in I&C cables.

Mechanical enclosures such as cubicles, racks and panels used for I&C systems shall conform to the relevant sections of IEC 60297: Part 3 for uniformity of dimensions and arrangements. The degree of protection for indoor cubicles and panels shall be IP42 minimum while those located outdoor in plant areas shall be IP54 minimum. The cubicles and panels shall be mounted in such a manner as to minimise external vibration being transmitted to internal components, for which suitable anti-vibration mounting arrangements (e.g. anti-vibration pads) shall be used.
The earthing scheme proposed for I&C systems shall reduce the effects of electrical/electromagnetic interference and ensure the safety of personnel. All metallic parts of cubicles and panels including doors shall be earthed by earthing conductors/braids of suitable cross-section using serrated washers to ensure a positive contact. Cable screens shall be terminated in such a way that earth loops are not introduced. Cable screens shall be terminated only at one end for which an insulated 'clean' earth bar shall be provided in cubicles. The earth bar shall be connected to the site earth via the cubicle safety earth at a single point. Armoured cables when used shall have their armours connected together externally, but shall be electrically isolated from the cubicles. The cable armours shall be connected to the site earth at a single point.
The layout of the interior of cubicles, junction boxes and panels shall facilitate easy access to components and terminals during commissioning and maintenance. In general, 10% of spare capacity shall be provided as a minimum in cubicles, panels, racks and junction boxes. This shall include unused module slots, unallocated wired I/O channels, unused terminals, space for additional external cables etc. The spare capacity of 10% shall be made available by Contractor after final commissioning which shall be pre-engineered, implemented, terminated and ready for use.
If forced ventilation is to be used in cubicles and panels, 100% redundant fans shall be employed with facilities for fan failure detection and alarming on the DCMS. Thermostatically controlled anti-condensation heaters shall be installed in cubicles and panels. Maintenance facilities such as internal lighting and a power socket shall also be provided in cubicles and panels.
Labels or other suitable identification methods shall be provided for sub-assemblies and terminals in cubicles and panels. This shall include modules, racks, power supplies, pre-fabricated cables, I/O termination boards, external cables and their conductors, terminals etc. A 'danger' label shall be provided with shroud for terminals connecting 110 V and above.

Any cement to be used for concrete piles shall be in accordance with the CIRIA guide and ASTM C150 latest edition. It shall be assumed that all Plant mechanical, electrical and control equipment will require access for maintenance purposes periodically during the life of the Plant. The following general criteria shall be used as a guideline for locating devices either as singular components or packaged systems from vendors:
- one person without hindered access can lift about 30 kg
- two persons each without hindered access can lift about 45 kg
If access is hindered or weights are greater than 45 kg, means of lifting like permanent monorail, lifting beams and hoists with a chain block or via chain fall, or with fork-lift with unicorn attachment, or in the event of special cases, mobile (any mobile crane or fork-lift post COD is to be provided by the Owner) or permanent cranes shall be anticipated. In the case of some electrical equipment, trolleys or special handling gear are available from the Contractor and these should be included in the Work if other means are not available.
Disassembly of components into sub-assemblies shall not generally be accepted as a means around the weights above. For instance, while it is acceptable to take the diaphragm operator and yoke off a control valve as a sub assembly, it is not acceptable to break the diaphragm operator into several pieces for meeting the weight criteria.
A clear identified path from the device to a maintenance corridor for hauling/transport purposes shall be specifically identified if not obvious from the arrangement. If the device is at an elevated location in the Plant, a clear method of getting the component to a service platform or road shall be identified if not obvious.
Where mobile cranes are required for maintenance purposes, there shall be specific plans to identify placement of the crane and specific make and model rigs shall be identified for the duty. Use of greatly over capacity rigs for light components because of long reach shall generally be avoided.
Back clearance from the work face area shall be a minimum of 600 mm at a point, and preferably be greater than 750mm. In the case of pumps (or other rotating equipment), these clearances should be maintained on each side of the pump centreline. An unobstructed path from the work area to a plant maintenance corridor shall be established in the plant design.

The Contractor shall provide the O&M manuals for review including all information necessary for the safe, secure and economical operation and maintenance of the Power Plant.
The content of O&M documents shall be in compliance with the relevant practice and industrial requirements and subject to Owner's approval.
The operational and maintenance documentation shall cover the whole Plant and all systems and equipment one by one within the scope of Work.
The manuals shall include items such as :
- operation instructions
- maintenance instructions
- equipment lists, settings, etc
- drawings, diagrams , etc
- spare parts, special tools

chunks.text:
The operation instructions shall include operational situation such as:
- preparations for start-up
- start-up
- operation in power and heat generation
- shut-down
- disturbance situations
- standstill and preparation for maintenance
- preservation
As far as applicable, the following items may also be included in the operational instructions:
- technical structure and functioning of the system in question
- theoretical background of functioning of the system concerned
- electrical part of the system/equipment
- automation/instrumentation part of the system/equipment
- water and steam part system/equipment
- steam/water chemistry
- material questions
- operational limits for measured values
- modes of operation to be avoided, if any, and the reason for restrictions
- precautions to be taken for normal and abnormal operating conditions
The operational instructions may include photographs, videos, drawings, pictures, functional diagrams and other material necessary for understanding and visualization of the instructions.
The operational instructions shall be divided according to the above operational situations of each individual system so that the above items are included in each operational situation.

The details of the training program shall be agreed between the Contractor and Owner's.
Emphasize shall be on 'on-the-job' training and instruction for O&M personnel and building up the training programs (2 separate training tracks for operation staff and 1 for maintenance staff) accommodating O&M staff's mobilisation program.
All programs will be scheduled for a normal 5 day works week, excluding holidays observed by the Owner. Due to the technical content of the programs, instruction will be limited to 8 hours per day.
The Contractor shall advise the Owner of all sub-contractor representatives on site to allow the Owner's personnel to co-ordinate and receive on-the-job-training.
Here below is highlighted the overall framework and philosophy the O&M training should be based on when Contractor starts to plan the detailed training program for the Owner's O&M personnel.
O&M Operator's personnel shall be trained in due time by the Contractor to prepare them both in theory and practice for the management, operation and maintenance of all parts of the Plant.
Each site personnel shall be included in Overviews and Operation training.
English language shall be used for all training purposes.
The aim of the training is to teach the operation and maintenance personnel of the Owner to such an extent that after completion of the training they are able to:
- safely and economically operate the Power Plant with all its auxiliaries without the support of the Contractor
- carry out regular daily and weekly maintenance routines independently and in a correct way
- carry out maintenance and repair works independently and in a correct way
Also 'system walk-downs' with groups of 6 or less students shall be conducted to familiarize the student with the physical location of the equipment and acquaint the student with system an equipment features, controls, and displays. If possible actual operations, routine maintenance and routine checks of all equipment shall be demonstrated.
In addition to the above classroom training, an essential part of the training shall be the participation in the operation and maintenance during the commissioning phase of the Plant. The trainees will obtain real experience by attending the Plant operations under the supervision of the Contractor's commissioning engineer. The personnel will become familiar e.g. with remote/local control and monitoring, equipment operations as well as with the technical characteristics of the Plant. Detailed plan including shift schedule for the same shall be pre-agreed between the Contractor, Owner and Operator 180 days prior to start-up of any commissioning activities in the plant.
Training shall be provided by the Contractor's commissioning team and/or a nominated professional training team. The Contractor shall nominate a training coordinator. The training documents shall be based on the Plant instruction manuals. Drawings / schematics of the Plant shall be extensively used in the training.
